findings.reason: a coordinator reading this plan alone can dispatch §6 beside sn-audited-group-release#s4 (still implementable) and get two blind audits of 208 members and two release candidates for one group.
findings.text: §6 regenerates equilibrium, adjudicates it and cuts its release candidate to the fork, which is the whole deliverable of sn-audited-group-release#s4 ("every member of the first group is audited, not sampled... and the group's release candidate is cut"), yet §6 declares only sn-audited-group-release#s3 and neither depends on #s4 nor states that it supersedes it

findings.reason: the hold-kind retirement is a data migration with its own failure mode and needs its own section or a control that a held name losing its hold is refused; as written it is closed by a gate that never looks at it.
findings.text: §4's done-when carries two deliverables, generation-or-blocker per name and the consolidation of blockers into the existing hold store with "any existing hold kind it replaces retired", and only "named in the evidence" stands behind the retirement, so a migration that silently drops the holds it replaces closes on the same verdict as the generation behaviour

findings.reason: a node given no path writes these where it runs, so the benchmark's per-arm figures and the two suite logs become unopenable and the reuse of the case files in §3 and §4 loses its provenance.
findings.text: §2, §3 and §4 require recorded runs, a token-size distribution, per-arm tables and head-against-base suite logs on a compute partition, and name no path, while §1, §5 and §6 all name docs/evidence/fragments/sn-case-file-generation/
